messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGM Dyadic Covariate Issue
messages.body_plain:
Maureen,

Given the number of terms in your model, and esp. the number of 
dyadic-dependent terms, relative to the information in your data (11 
replicates of 81 tie variables), I'm guessing one problem is that you 
don't have enough data to fit all of these terms.  I'd be worried in 
particular about the combination of twopaths and 2star terms here, as 
these types of terms tend to be less stable in small nets.

But in the first example, the 1.0 correlation between the edges and 
dyadcov suggests you have a more basic problem. Since I can't see what is 
in Behaviors_matrix.csv file, I can't replicate what you have, but see if 
your dyadcov is identical (or nearly identical) to your outcome variable 
by running a correlation on them alone.

Have you tried to fit some smaller models, and then build up the 
additional terms to see when the problem arises?

best,
Martina

On Wed, 26 Aug 2015, Maureen McCusker wrote:

> Hi there,
> My name is Maureen McCusker, and I?m a graduate student at Virginia Tech, earning my Ph.D. in I/O Psychology. First of
> all, thank you for making yourselves available. I am writing to you because I have been working on on a project running
> an ERGM model for several months and have been struggling with my dyadic covariate term. To give you a little background,
> I am analyzing some data on dyadic leadership perceptions within 11 teams of 9, where the outcome is a dichotomous
> rating. In addition to several other predictors in the model (icov, ocov, absdiff), my model includes 2 edcov terms: the
> structural zero matrix, reflecting the teams, and the directed dyadic covariate. I have seen the dyadic covariate matrix
> read into R using run using two different codes, and I am receiving error codes for both (please see below). ?I am
> wondering if you might be able to tell me which is the correct R code for dyadic covariates, and for the correct one,
> what the error code means.
> 
> For the following code, Beh is the dyadic covariate term. 
> 
> 1. The first code I?m using simply reads the data in as a CSV, converts it to a matrix, and then converts it to a
> network. In the ERGM code itself, I run the network in as an edcov term (see this below). When I run this method, the
> dyadic covariate term is HIGHLY unstable and changes values as signs with a slight change in the parameters, such MCMC
> sample size. I also receive a message stating that I likely have highly correlated terms, which is what I assume is
> driving the instability in the dyadic covariate term. When I check MCMC Diagnostics, I find that the dyadic covariate and
> the edges term are perfectly correlated at 1.0. I know there have been some recent findings that ERGM may have some
> issues with small groups and also that there are potentially some problems with highly correlated model terms. If this is
> the correct way to run the dyadic covariate term, do you have any ideas of how I can fix this issue? ?R Code: 
> 
> #reading behavior file
> 
> Beh?<- read.csv("Behaviors_Matrix.csv",?header?=?FALSE)
> 
> Beh.mat1<-as.matrix(Beh)
> 
> Beh.mat2<-apply(Beh.mat1,1,as.numeric)
> 
> Beh.mat2[is.na(Beh.mat2)]<-0
> 
> Beh.mat2
> 
> Beh.net?<-as.network.matrix(Beh.mat2,directed=T,matrix.type="adjacency?)
> 
> And then here is the ERGM: 
> 
> New_Model_2_beh_2<-ergm(DV.net?~edges+ostar(2)+?mutual?+?twopath?+ istar(2) + edgecov(Struc_Zero.net) +
> edgecov(tasks.net)+ nodeocov("Dom")+nodeocov("Self_Eff")+nodeicov("SAT_Tot") +nodeicov("Dom") +nodeicov("Self_Eff")
> +nodeicov("Self_Mon") + absdiff("Self_Mon")+absdiff("Dom") +dyadcov(Beh.net),?eval.loglik=TRUE,??seed=20,?burnin=2000,?interval=50,?MCMCsamplesize=100000,?maxit=10,?control=control
> .ergm(steplength=.25))
> 
> summary(New_Model_2_beh_2)
> 
> 2. The second way I?m running the model is similar to the way that another?researcher, who I know also posted on
> Statnet_help?regarding a similar issue back in?February, ran hers.?When I do it this way, I receive the same error
> message she received (In m[tl[!nal] + (hl[!nal] - 1) * network.size(x)] <- val[!nal] : number of items to replace is not
> a multiple of replacement length). Using this strategy, I first create a megamatrix of all possible ties, then I run in a
> matrix of all the dyadic ?attributes? to assign to the ties, then I assign attributes to the ?all-possible ties" matrix.
> The edgecov term in the ERGM is also different. Please see below: 
> 
> #reading behavior file
> Beh?<- read.csv("Behaviors_Matrix.csv",?header?=?FALSE)
> Beh.mat1<-as.matrix(Beh)
> Beh.mat2<-apply(Beh.mat1,1,as.numeric)
> Beh.mat2[is.na(Beh.mat2)]<-0 
> Beh.mat2
> Beh.net?<-as.network.matrix(Beh.mat2,directed=T,matrix.type="adjacency")
> summary(Beh.net)
> 
> #making all possible ties matrix: 
> Poss_ties<- read.csv("poss_ties_mat2.csv",?header?=?FALSE) 
> Poss_ties.mat1<-as.matrix(Poss_ties)
> Poss_ties.mat2<-apply(Poss_ties.mat1,?1,?as.numeric)
> Poss_ties.net<-as.network.matrix(Poss_ties,directed=F,matrix.type="adjacency?)
> 
> #assigning behaviors to possible ties 
> set.edge.attribute(Poss_ties.net,"Beh.net",Beh.net)
> 
> The ERGM for strategy 2 is then as follows: 
> New_Model_2<-ergm(DV.net?~edges+ostar(2)+?mutual?+?twopath?+?istar(2)?+?edgecov(tasks.net)?+?edgecov(Poss_ties.net,attrn
> ame="Beh.net")+?edgecov(Struc_Zero.net)?+?nodeocov("Dom")+nodeocov("Self_Eff")+nodeicov("SAT_Tot")?+nodeicov("Dom")?+nod
> eicov("Self_Eff")?+nodeicov("Self_Mon")?+?absdiff("Self_Mon")+absdiff("Dom"),?eval.loglik=TRUE,??seed=20,?burnin=3000,?i
> nterval=50,?MCMCsamplesize=50000,?maxit=10,?control=control.ergm(steplength=.25))
> 
> As you can see, for both of these strategies, I employ a structural zero matrix. The structural zero matrix has given me
> problems since i started because the output because the output produces a ?-INF? estimate and NA for standard errors.
> Perhaps this is part of the issue. 
> 
> 
> Thank you in advance for your help.
> 
> Maureen 
>

In the continuing discussion over how to interpret the gw* terms, here is 
the latest contribution, courtesy of Steve Goodreau and Sam Jenness. 
Attached are a couple of slides from a workshop, and below some 
accompanying explanation.

best,
Martina

     SAMUEL MACLEAN JENNESS <sjenness@uw.edu>

Yes! These really help a lot. Thanks for attaching them.

On Wed, Sep 9, 2015 at 4:16 PM, martina morris <morrism@u.washington.edu> wrote:
       Hi Andrew,

       The numerical value of the summary will depend on the value you use for
       alpha.? If you fix it at zero, it is the count of edges (for gwesp) that
       are in at least one triangle.? As alpha increases the value asymptotes at
       the number of edges in a triangle (so 3 x # triangles).? For dsp, just
       substitute dyads with shared partners.

       We've just put together a brief explanation for a workshop, and I'm
       attaching the relevant slides here.? LMK if they help.

       best,
       mm

       > Hi Dr. Morris,

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Specifying missing/unobserved edges in a network object
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statnet Developers,

I am looking for ways to apply ergms to model unobserved ties in a network. Say I have a sample of 50 nodes (numbered consecutively from 1 to 50), and I know there are 75 edges between them. However, I only observe 50 edges, between the first 30 nodes. I want to specify that there are 25 possible edges between nodes 31:50, which are ?missing?.

How can I create a network object that includes a specification for the missing edges?
Thanks,
Aditya

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Complex ERG Model
messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet community,

I recently acquired data from an online political debate network, and I 
would like to analyze it with a somewhat complex erg model. The network 
comprises 3 different directed link types, which I want to analyze like 
separate networks. Furthermore, I want to distinguish between 3 
different political situations (before elections, before referenda, and 
other periods; each situation comprises several different time 
intervals). Basically, I am interested in comparing the strength of 
several homophily parameters a) across the 3 different linkstypes and b) 
across the 3 different situations. Basically, my hpothesis is that 
homophily will be strongest before elections and weakest before 
referenda, and that this effect in turn varies with link type. I already 
implemented this model as a logistic regression, by simply merging the 
dyad lists of all 9  combinations of the 3 link types and 3 situations, 
and including them as dummy variables. The outcomes supported my 
hypotheses, but now I would like to see if I can reproduce them in an 
ergm including parameters for reciprocity and triadic closure. At the 
moment, however, I am only able to do this by computing a separate ergm 
for each of the 9 combinations. This is of course also problematic since 
it ignores that a link formed in one period might form a triad with a 
two-path from a previous period. Additionally, while I can rertieve 
homophily parameters from every combination and compare them, I have no 
comprehensive test of whether they really vary in strength according to 
my hypotheses. I would be very glad for hints of how to combine this in 
one big model - Thanks!

Simon Schweighofer,
PhD candidate at Chair of Systems Design,
ETH Zurich
